message.content: {"caption":"A prompt panel listing a programming agent’s recommended workflow and cautions.","description":"A wide, rounded rectangular panel with a dark teal header labeled “Main Agent Prompt” and a light gray body containing small monospaced text. The body begins, “As a professional and experienced programmer, your approach is to:” and presents a numbered workflow: slow down rather than write whole files end-to-end at once; understand the project by finding and reviewing useful documentation and relevant code; optionally prototype or design before coding, using simple test-directory examples and execution feedback; make minimal effective code edits while following existing style; test end-to-end, preferably without a test framework unless the project already uses one, and check for regressions; then update documentation and remove temporary files or changes. A final “NOTE” section says not to create virtual environments, to avoid pytest and mocks where possible in favor of end-to-end scripts, that clearly exploratory requests may bypass the rigorous procedure, and to call a reasoning agent for help with a tricky algorithmic or mathematical problem. There are no arrows, diagrams, or chart marks.","figure_type":"screenshot","chart_values":[]}
